entries.name: Anthropic Python SDK
entries.use_for: Call Claude models from Python: messages, streaming, tool use, batches
entries.why: Official Python client for the Claude API; counterpart to the TS SDK already listed, typed and kept in step with the API
entries.summary: Official Python client for the Claude API: messages, streaming, tool helpers (@beta_tool and the tool runner), browser and computer toolsets, and OpenTelemetry spans per API call.
entries.best_for: Calling Claude from Python.
entries.not_for: Claude only. For multiple providers use LiteLLM or a framework; agent loops need the Agent SDK or your own code.

entries.name: Anthropic TypeScript SDK
entries.use_for: Official TypeScript client for the Anthropic Claude API, including streaming and tool use.
entries.why: Official vendor SDK for Claude, typed end to end and updated alongside API releases.
entries.summary: Official TypeScript client for the Claude API: streaming, structured outputs, tool helpers and tool runner, browser and computer toolsets. Supports Node 20+, Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge.
entries.best_for: Server-side TS/JS apps calling Claude.
entries.not_for: Browser use is disabled by default (dangerouslyAllowBrowser required) to avoid exposing keys. Claude only; React Native not supported.

entries.name: apfel
entries.use_for: Use the LLM built into Apple Silicon Macs from the shell or through a local OpenAI-compatible server.
entries.why: Free, on-device and keyless, wrapping Apple FoundationModels as a UNIX tool and server.
entries.summary: A Swift tool that exposes Apple's built-in on-device model as a pipe-friendly command and a local OpenAI-compatible server, with an interactive chat. Nothing leaves the machine and no API key is needed.
entries.best_for: Quick local scripting and prototypes on a Mac with no key, cloud or download.
entries.not_for: Anything needing a big model, embeddings or other platforms. macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon, one roughly 3B model, 4096-token context on many Macs.

entries.name: Ax
entries.use_for: Build LLM programs with DSPy-style signatures and automatic prompt optimization in TypeScript.
entries.why: The most complete DSPy port for TypeScript; supports many providers and typed signatures instead of hand-written prompts.
entries.summary: DSPy-style library for TypeScript: typed signatures (string DSL or Zod/Valibot/ArkType), agents, flows as typed graphs and optimizers such as GEPA, across many providers. Also generated for Python, Java, C++, Go and Rust.
entries.best_for: TypeScript LLM programs with typed signatures and automatic prompt optimization.
entries.not_for: Other language ports are generated libraries; smaller community than DSPy. Needs eval data to benefit from optimizers.

entries.name: BitNet
entries.use_for: Run 1-bit (ternary) LLMs fast on CPUs and GPUs
entries.why: Microsoft's official inference framework for BitNet b1.58 models; optimized kernels make large models usable on commodity CPUs.
entries.summary: Official inference framework (bitnet.cpp) for 1-bit LLMs such as BitNet b1.58, with optimized CPU kernels (and a GPU kernel) for fast, lossless inference; also supports 1-bit embedding models.
entries.best_for: Running 1.58-bit models efficiently on CPUs or edge hardware.
entries.not_for: Only for BitNet-type models, not arbitrary open LLMs (use llama.cpp). NPU support is described as coming.

entries.name: codex-chatgpt-web
entries.use_for: Use your ChatGPT Web models, including Pro, from inside Codex's model picker.
entries.why: Uses ChatGPT Web's separate limits, and full harness mode links its tool calls back to the Codex task over MCP.
entries.summary: A launcher that adds ChatGPT Web models to Codex's native model picker, using an embedded browser signed in to ChatGPT. Full harness mode connects ChatGPT to the current task's files, terminal, tools and approvals through MCP via an outbound tunnel, keeping conversations tied to the Codex task.
entries.best_for: Codex users who want ChatGPT Web model quota instead of spending Codex quota.
entries.not_for: Anyone who wants an official, supported route. It drives the ChatGPT web UI, and available models depend on your account.

entries.name: colibri
entries.use_for: Run very large mixture-of-experts open models on ordinary hardware by streaming experts from disk.
entries.why: Pure C with no dependencies and no GPU needed, with a dashboard showing experts as they fire.
entries.summary: colibri is an inference engine that keeps the dense part of a MoE model in RAM and reads routed experts from disk through a learning cache. It has thirteen engines, one per model family, including GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek and Qwen. A GPU is optional.
entries.best_for: You want to try or study huge open MoE models on a laptop or modest server.
entries.not_for: Speed depends on RAM, disk and cache. Each model family has its own engine, so support is limited to the listed ones.

entries.name: DwarfStar (ds4)
entries.use_for: Run DeepSeek V4 Flash and a few other large models locally on a Mac or CUDA/ROCm GPUs.
entries.why: A small native engine tuned for a few models, with SSD streaming and multi-GPU serving.
entries.summary: DwarfStar is a narrow native inference engine, first tuned for DeepSeek V4 Flash, plus GLM and Qwen models. It uses its own GGUF files, with Metal, CUDA and ROCm backends. It has an HTTP server, a coding agent and tools for quality and speed tests.
entries.best_for: Running a few big open models well on a MacBook, DGX Spark, Strix Halo or CUDA cards.
entries.not_for: A general GGUF runner. It only loads the project's own GGUF files, and the README says it is beta quality.

entries.name: edge0
entries.use_for: Run large mixture-of-experts models on laptops and phones by streaming experts from SSD.
entries.why: Memory use depends on the active experts, not total parameters, with a router that predicts loads.
entries.summary: A streaming MoE inference framework that combines SSD expert offload, Recover-LoRA and a prerouter that predicts which experts load next. It has a transformers-style Python API and engines for macOS, iOS and Android, with preview model checkpoints.
entries.best_for: Running big sparse models on consumer hardware with little RAM.
entries.not_for: Server throughput serving. The CUDA backend is only a reserved slot, and the iOS, macOS and Android engines use separate platform stacks.

entries.name: FreeToken
entries.use_for: Run very large open-weight MoE models locally on a gaming PC.
entries.why: Uses CPU-GPU co-execution, expert caching and semantic KV checkpoints to make huge MoE models usable at home.
entries.summary: FreeToken is an edge-native serving engine for Mixture-of-Experts models on personal hardware. It splits work between GPU and CPU, streams prefill layers, caches experts, and avoids recomputing context after agentic edits. It supports models like DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen and GLM, and comes as a desktop app and a CLI.
entries.best_for: Running frontier-scale MoE models locally with limited VRAM.
entries.not_for: Dense models or macOS. The desktop download is for Windows or Linux, and it targets MoE models.

entries.name: GLM-5 series
entries.use_for: Use open-weights GLM-5.x models for coding and long-horizon agent tasks, locally or via the Z.ai API.
entries.why: GLM-5.2 offers a 1M-token context and GLM-5.3 is described as the strongest open-weights model for coding.
entries.summary: The GLM-5 family of Z.ai flagship models: GLM-5, 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 with a Flash variant. They target coding, agentic engineering and long tasks. They can be used through the Z.ai API or by running the open weights.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting an open-weights model for coding agents, with a hosted API as a fallback.
entries.not_for: Benchmark claims come from the vendor. Running the large models needs serious GPU hardware.

entries.name: Google Gen AI SDK (JS)
entries.use_for: Call Gemini models from TypeScript/JavaScript, incl. Live API and Vertex AI
entries.why: Official unified Gemini SDK for JS (replaces @google/generative-ai); covers both the Gemini API and Vertex AI
entries.summary: Official Google Gen AI SDK for TypeScript/JavaScript to call Gemini via the Gemini Developer API or Vertex AI, including Live API. Notes upcoming changes to automatic function calling and Node 22+ in v3.
entries.best_for: JS/TS apps using Gemini models.
entries.not_for: Google-only; v3 will require Node 22 and change AFC behavior, so pin <3.0.0 if needed. Avoid exposing API keys client-side.

entries.name: Google Gen AI SDK (Python)
entries.use_for: Call Gemini models from Python against the Gemini API or Vertex AI
entries.why: Official unified Python SDK for Gemini; the supported replacement for google-generativeai
entries.summary: Official Google Gen AI Python SDK for Gemini via the Gemini Developer API or Vertex AI, including Live API and video generation. Replaces google-generativeai; the README warns of breaking changes to AFC and Live methods.
entries.best_for: Python apps calling Gemini.
entries.not_for: Google-only; upcoming major version removes several methods, so pin <3.0.0 to avoid breakage.

entries.name: Hugging Face JS
entries.use_for: Call Hugging Face Inference Providers and the Hub from JavaScript
entries.why: Official JS client for HF inference (many providers behind one API) and Hub access
entries.summary: Collection of JS libraries for the Hugging Face ecosystem: hub (repos, files), inference (Inference Providers and Endpoints), mcp-client, gguf parser, jinja, tasks and more, all typed.
entries.best_for: Calling HF models or managing Hub repos from JS/TS, or parsing GGUF remotely.
entries.not_for: Hub-centric; for local inference use other runtimes. Some packages are niche.

entries.name: Instructor
entries.use_for: Get validated, typed structured outputs from any LLM via Pydantic models
entries.why: Most widely used structured-output layer for LLMs; works across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and local models
entries.summary: Structured-output library that returns validated Pydantic objects from LLMs, with retries on validation errors and a unified from_provider interface across providers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini.
entries.best_for: Reliable typed extraction from LLM responses with minimal code.
entries.not_for: Extraction-focused; for agents and observability use PydanticAI. Python-first, relying on provider tool/JSON modes plus validation retries.

entries.name: Kimi K3
entries.use_for: Use or self-host an open-weight multimodal model for coding, agents and long-context work.
entries.why: An open-weight 2.8T-parameter model with native vision and a 1M-token context window.
entries.summary: Kimi K3 is an open-weight, native multimodal agentic model with 2.8T parameters. It uses Kimi Delta Attention and a mixture-of-experts design that activates 16 of 896 experts. Thinking is always on, and the API returns `reasoning_content`.
entries.best_for: Teams that want frontier-class open weights for long coding sessions, research and tool use.
entries.not_for: Weights fall under the Kimi K3 License, not a standard open license. Multi-turn use must pass back full assistant messages including reasoning. A model this size needs serious hardware.

entries.name: kimi-k3-in-c
entries.use_for: Study or run Kimi K3 inference in plain C99 on a CPU with very little RAM.
entries.why: A 176 KB engine with no BLAS, framework or GPU, tested against a PyTorch reference.
entries.summary: A portable C99 inference engine for the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3. It streams the checkpoint from disk, so peak memory is about 8 GB. Output is byte-identical across machines; more RAM only speeds it up. A weightless test suite builds in about a minute.
entries.best_for: Learning how a huge mixture-of-experts model runs, or running it offline on ordinary hardware when speed does not matter.
entries.not_for: Very slow on small machines (about 26 s per token with 8 GB RAM). Needs a 1.56 TB checkpoint on fast disk. Not for production serving.

entries.name: KTransformers
entries.use_for: Run huge MoE LLMs locally with hybrid CPU/GPU offloading
entries.why: Heterogeneous inference that runs DeepSeek-class MoE models on a single GPU plus system RAM; exposes OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.summary: Research framework for CPU-GPU heterogeneous inference and fine-tuning of large MoE LLMs, with AMX/AVX-optimized CPU kernels, NUMA-aware memory, INT4/INT8 quantization and SGLang integration; supports LoRA fine-tuning.
entries.best_for: Running very large MoE models like DeepSeek-class on a single GPU plus lots of system RAM.
entries.not_for: Research-grade and hardware-specific (best with Intel AMX/AVX512 and large RAM); not for small models or turnkey serving.

entries.name: Laya
entries.use_for: Get typed choice, score or yes/no decisions over any text in one fast forward pass.
entries.why: A non-autoregressive model that answers in about 33 ms across 100+ languages, with a checkpoint router.
entries.summary: Laya is a decision engine, not a text generator. You give it text and typed questions, such as which department should handle a ticket, and it returns choices or scores in a single forward pass. A router picks the right checkpoint per request. It has Python and Rust SDKs.
entries.best_for: Routing, triage and classification tasks where an LLM call is too slow or costly.
entries.not_for: Does not write free text. Long-document accuracy varies beyond about 4,000 tokens, so test on your own data.

entries.name: LiteLLM
entries.use_for: Call 100+ LLM APIs through one OpenAI-format interface, as a Python SDK or a self-hosted gateway.
entries.why: Widely adopted unified client/proxy with cost tracking, fallbacks and rate limits; MIT outside its enterprise/ folder.
entries.summary: Python SDK and self-hosted AI Gateway giving one OpenAI-format interface to 100+ LLM providers. Proxy adds virtual keys, spend tracking, guardrails, load balancing and admin UI; supports chat, responses, embeddings, images, audio and more.
entries.best_for: Provider-agnostic LLM calls or a central gateway with cost tracking and fallbacks.
entries.not_for: An enterprise folder and tier is separately licensed; running the proxy adds infrastructure. SDK-only users may not need the gateway.

entries.name: LitGPT
entries.use_for: Pretrain, finetune and serve 20+ open LLMs with simple recipes
entries.why: Lightning AI's hackable from-scratch implementations of popular LLMs with LoRA/QLoRA, FSDP and serving recipes.
entries.summary: From-scratch, readable implementations of 20+ LLMs with recipes to pretrain, fine-tune (LoRA, QLoRA, adapters) and deploy, with Flash Attention, FSDP, quantization and configs for 1 to 1000+ GPUs.
entries.best_for: Learning, hacking or fine-tuning open LLMs with simple, transparent code.
entries.not_for: Not an optimized production server (use vLLM). Focus is on supported model architectures.

entries.name: llama.cpp
entries.use_for: Run open-weight LLMs locally on CPU/GPU with GGUF models and an OpenAI-compatible server
entries.why: The engine under Ollama, LM Studio and most local-LLM tools; broadest hardware and model support
entries.summary: C/C++ LLM and VLM inference with no dependencies, using GGUF models and quantization from 1.5 to 8 bits on a wide hardware range (Apple silicon, x86, RISC-V, GPUs). Includes a CLI, OpenAI-compatible server and web UI.
entries.best_for: Running open-weight models locally on CPU or GPU, or embedding inference in native apps.
entries.not_for: Lower-level than Ollama; models must be GGUF. Not designed for maximum multi-user GPU throughput (vLLM).

entries.name: llmfit
entries.use_for: Check which open LLMs your CPU, RAM and GPU can actually run, and how fast.
entries.why: Scores hundreds of models on fit, speed, quality and context, with a TUI, web dashboard and REST API.
entries.summary: llmfit detects your CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then scores a catalog of models across quantizations for memory fit, estimated speed, quality and context. It has an interactive terminal UI, a CLI, a web dashboard and a JSON API. Users can also share benchmarks.
entries.best_for: Picking a local model before you download it, or adding hardware-aware model choice to a deployment script.
entries.not_for: It recommends models; it does not run inference. Speed numbers are estimates unless you benchmark on your own machine.

entries.name: LM Studio SDK
entries.use_for: Load and call local models running in LM Studio from TypeScript.
entries.why: Official SDK for LM Studio, with model management, structured output and tool use against local models.
entries.summary: Official LM Studio TypeScript SDK to chat with local models, define tools for local agents, load/configure/unload models, use embeddings and structured output, in Node or browser.
entries.best_for: JS/TS apps controlling models running in LM Studio.
entries.not_for: Requires LM Studio running; unlike the OpenAI SDK it is not for hosted providers. Major versions had breaking changes.

entries.name: Magnitude
entries.use_for: Run open models locally with kernels tuned to your hardware, and connect them to your coding agent.
entries.why: The README claims over 2x faster than Ollama across popular local models on Mac and NVIDIA.
entries.summary: An open-source inference engine that tunes its kernels for each model on your hardware. It ships as a desktop app with a CLI and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or CPU. It adds speculative decoding drafters and one-click links to agents like Pi, OpenCode and Codex.
entries.best_for: Running local models for agents with better speed than a default setup.
entries.not_for: Speed figures are the project's own. Model size is limited by your memory.

entries.name: Mesh LLM
entries.use_for: Pool GPUs and memory across machines and serve one OpenAI-compatible API for local or shared models.
entries.why: Large models can be split across nodes, and the mesh decides whether to run locally or route to a peer.
entries.summary: Mesh LLM joins machines into one inference mesh with an OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:9337. You can start with one node and add more, and join a public mesh or run a private one. Skippy handles model management and split execution.
entries.best_for: People with several consumer machines who want to run models too big for one box, or share compute with others.
entries.not_for: A single-machine setup where plain llama.cpp or Ollama is enough. Windows multi-node LAN clustering may need WSL2.

entries.name: Mini-SGLang
entries.use_for: Serve LLMs with a small readable engine, or learn how modern serving systems work.
entries.why: About 5,000 lines of typed Python with radix cache, chunked prefill and FlashAttention.
entries.summary: A compact version of SGLang with radix cache, chunked prefill, overlap scheduling, tensor parallelism and FlashAttention/FlashInfer kernels. It launches an OpenAI-compatible server with one command.
entries.best_for: Researchers and engineers who want to read, modify or learn from an LLM serving engine.
entries.not_for: Windows or macOS: it is Linux only and needs the CUDA toolkit. For full features use the main SGLang project.

entries.name: Mistral TypeScript SDK
entries.use_for: Call Mistral models (chat, embeddings, OCR, agents) from TypeScript
entries.why: Official Mistral client for TypeScript
entries.summary: Official TypeScript client for Mistral AI: chat, embeddings, OCR, agents and prompts. v2 is ESM-only with Zod v4, shorter type names and a migration guide.
entries.best_for: Calling Mistral models from TS/JS.
entries.not_for: Mistral-only. v2 is ESM-only and has breaking changes from v1.

entries.name: MNN
entries.use_for: Run LLMs and other models on-device on mobile, embedded and desktop
entries.why: Alibaba's battle-tested lightweight inference engine; powers on-device LLMs in production apps with CPU/GPU/NPU backends.
entries.summary: Lightweight deep learning framework for on-device inference and training with CPU/GPU/NPU backends, used in 30+ Alibaba apps. Supports LLMs (Qwen series), vision-language models and has a Hexagon DSP backend; includes a Workbench and mobile chat apps.
entries.best_for: Deploying LLMs and other models on mobile, embedded and IoT devices.
entries.not_for: Requires converting/exporting models to MNN; ecosystem smaller than PyTorch/ONNX. Documentation partly China-focused.

entries.name: Needle
entries.use_for: Run tool calls, structured extraction, embeddings and speech on phones and tiny devices with an 8-29 MB model.
entries.why: A single small binary that beats much larger models on mobile tool calls and guarantees parseable output.
entries.summary: Needle is a very small foundation model for mobiles, wearables, robots, smart homes, cars and microcontrollers. It picks the right tool and fills its arguments, extracts typed fields from messy text under a schema grammar, and returns embeddings. A sibling model, Whistle, adds speech input. It installs with pip.
entries.best_for: On-device assistants and automation where size, latency and privacy matter.
entries.not_for: General chat. The README says it trades general chat capacity for tool calls and extraction.

entries.name: notebooklm-py
entries.use_for: Script Google's NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook) from Python, a CLI or an agent skill.
entries.why: Exposes features the web UI lacks, such as batch downloads and mind map JSON.
entries.summary: An unofficial Python API, CLI and agent skill for NotebookLM. It can bulk-import sources, run research queries, generate audio overviews, slides, quizzes and more, and download the results. It ships a skill for Claude Code and Codex.
entries.best_for: Research automation and agent workflows that use NotebookLM for grounded analysis.
entries.not_for: Production systems. It uses undocumented Google APIs that can change or be rate-limited without notice.

entries.name: Ollama
entries.use_for: Run open-weight LLMs locally behind a simple REST and OpenAI-compatible API.
entries.why: The most popular way to pull and serve local models; large model library and SDKs for JS and Python.
entries.summary: Runs open-weight models locally or in the cloud via a simple CLI, REST API (port 11434) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Includes a model library, JS and Python libraries, and ollama launch integrations for Claude Code, Codex and others.
entries.best_for: Easiest way to run and serve local models for dev tools and apps.
entries.not_for: Not for high-throughput multi-GPU serving (vLLM). Models come from its library or imports, and larger models need substantial hardware.

entries.name: oMLX
entries.use_for: Serve local LLMs on a Mac with continuous batching and a tiered memory and SSD KV cache.
entries.why: Keeps past context cached on SSD so agent tools like Claude Code stay fast.
entries.summary: oMLX is an inference server for Apple Silicon managed from the macOS menu bar. It supports text LLMs, vision models, OCR, embeddings and rerankers. It pins models in memory, swaps others in, and has a Homebrew install and a web UI.
entries.best_for: Mac users running local models for coding agents who want caching and model management.
entries.not_for: Windows, Linux or Nvidia GPUs; it targets Apple Silicon only.

entries.name: OpenAI Node SDK
entries.use_for: Official TypeScript/JavaScript client for the OpenAI API (chat, responses, embeddings, audio, images).
entries.why: Official vendor SDK, generated from the OpenAI API spec and kept in lockstep with new endpoints.
entries.summary: Official TypeScript/JavaScript client for the OpenAI API, generated from the OpenAPI spec. Primary API is Responses, with helpers like toResponseInputItems for multi-turn replay.
entries.best_for: Calling OpenAI from Node or TS, also usable with OpenAI-compatible servers.
entries.not_for: OpenAI-focused and low-level; agent features are in the separate Agents SDK. Do not expose keys in browsers.

entries.name: OpenAI Python SDK
entries.use_for: Official Python client for the OpenAI API, sync and async.
entries.why: Official vendor SDK; many OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio) accept it too, so one client covers many backends.
entries.summary: Official Python client for the OpenAI API with sync and async clients and full typings, generated from the OpenAPI spec. Responses API is primary; Chat Completions remains supported.
entries.best_for: Calling OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible backend from Python.
entries.not_for: OpenAI-specific and low-level; use the Agents SDK for orchestration. Requires Python 3.10+.

entries.name: OpenLLM
entries.use_for: Serve open-source LLMs as OpenAI-compatible API endpoints
entries.why: One command turns Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen etc. into an OpenAI-compatible server, built on BentoML for cloud deployment.
entries.summary: CLI that serves open-source LLMs (Llama, Qwen, Phi and custom models) as OpenAI-compatible APIs with one command, includes a chat UI, and deploys via Docker, Kubernetes or BentoCloud using BentoML.
entries.best_for: Quickly self-hosting open models behind an OpenAI-style endpoint with cloud deployment paths.
entries.not_for: Does not store weights (HF token for gated models); BentoML-tied. For maximum throughput use vLLM directly.

entries.name: Outlines
entries.use_for: Guarantee LLM output matches a JSON schema, regex or grammar
entries.why: Leading constrained-decoding library; its approach is used inside vLLM and other servers for structured generation
entries.summary: Guarantees LLM output matches a type, JSON schema, regex or grammar by constraining generation, via model(prompt, output_type) with Pydantic models and Literals. Works with OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM and others.
entries.best_for: Guaranteed-valid structured output, especially with local models.
entries.not_for: Strongest with local/self-hosted inference. For hosted APIs, simpler retry libraries like Instructor may suffice. The .txt API is early access.

entries.name: Rapid-MLX
entries.use_for: Serve local LLMs on a Mac with OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs and reliable tool calling.
entries.why: Faster decode than mlx-lm, oMLX and LM Studio in its own benchmarks, with continuous batching.
entries.summary: Rapid-MLX is an inference server for Apple Silicon built on MLX. It exposes OpenAI chat and responses endpoints and the Anthropic Messages API, focuses on tool calling for coding agents, and uses continuous batching. A macOS desktop app is also provided.
entries.best_for: You run models locally on a Mac and want coding agents to talk to them through standard APIs.
entries.not_for: Apple Silicon only. Speed numbers come from the project's own single-run benchmarks. Not for Linux or Windows servers.

entries.name: RLM
entries.use_for: Replace llm.completion with rlm.completion so a model can handle huge contexts by recursively calling itself in a REPL.
entries.why: Plug-and-play inference library for Recursive Language Models with local and cloud sandboxes.
entries.summary: Recursive Language Models let a model examine, split and recursively call itself over its input, with the context held as a variable in a REPL. The library supports a local REPL and isolated cloud sandboxes such as Prime and Modal.
entries.best_for: Researchers and builders working on very long-context tasks or CodeAct-style harnesses.
entries.not_for: The default local REPL is not safe for production or untrusted prompts. Use an isolated sandbox for that.

entries.name: SemIf
entries.use_for: Make fast typed yes/no or multi-option decisions from an open LLM by reading option probabilities directly.
entries.why: Skips generating text and parsing it back; scores typed options straight from model logits.
entries.summary: A research baseline that reproduces the 'semantic if' interface with open models. It takes unstructured state, runtime criteria and typed options, and reads option probabilities from a 4B model without an answer sentence or JSON repair. It runs on CUDA, Apple Silicon (MLX or MPS) or CPU through llama.cpp.
entries.best_for: Agent routing and small classification decisions where low latency and local models matter.
entries.not_for: An independent research project. It does not reproduce the closed Jev service's model or training.

entries.name: SenseNova-U1
entries.use_for: Run an open unified multimodal model for image understanding, generation and editing.
entries.why: One native model covers understanding, reasoning and generation, with native 4K and text-heavy infographics.
entries.summary: A series of native multimodal models that handle vision and language in a single architecture, without adapters. The U1.5-8B-MoT checkpoint targets image generation, text rendering, native 4K output and editing.
entries.best_for: Developers who want open image generation and editing with strong Chinese and English text rendering.
entries.not_for: Small GPUs or quick setups; these are large research checkpoints rather than a hosted API or lightweight SDK.

entries.name: Strata
entries.use_for: Run a very large open model on a gaming PC and call it through a local OpenAI/Anthropic-style API.
entries.why: One-click installer that fits a 125B-parameter model on a 12 GB GPU plus system RAM.
entries.summary: Strata is an inference engine that runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on consumer NVIDIA or AMD cards. It needs 12 GB of VRAM and 32 GB or more of RAM. It serves local OpenAI and Anthropic style APIs and can take image input.
entries.best_for: People who want private, local use of a large model with their coding agents on a Windows or Linux gaming PC.
entries.not_for: Running other models: it is built around one model family. Needs a strong GPU, lots of RAM and about 80 GB of disk.

entries.name: TanStack AI
entries.use_for: Type-safe, provider-agnostic TypeScript SDK for streaming chat, tool calling and agents.
entries.why: From the TanStack team; framework-agnostic and strongly typed, a lighter alternative to the Vercel AI SDK.
entries.summary: Type-safe, provider-agnostic TypeScript SDK for streaming chat, tool calling, structured output, realtime voice, media generation and agents, with React, Solid, Vue, Svelte, Preact bindings, devtools and OpenTelemetry. Code Mode lets an LLM run TypeScript in a sandbox.
entries.best_for: TS apps wanting a framework-agnostic alternative to the Vercel AI SDK with typed tools.
entries.not_for: Newer and smaller ecosystem than the Vercel AI SDK; adapters per provider are separate.

entries.name: TensorRT-LLM
entries.use_for: Optimize and serve LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs with a Python API
entries.why: NVIDIA's official LLM inference stack: in-flight batching, paged KV cache, FP8/FP4 quantization and speculative decoding for max GPU throughput.

license_verified.note: LICENSE states Apache 2.0 with third-party notices appended

entries.summary: NVIDIA's open library for optimized LLM inference on NVIDIA GPUs: custom kernels, in-flight batching, paged KV cache, FP8/FP4, speculative decoding, disaggregated prefill/decode, and a PyTorch-based Python LLM API from single GPU to multi-node.
entries.best_for: Maximum-throughput LLM serving on NVIDIA hardware.
entries.not_for: NVIDIA GPUs only; heavier setup than vLLM or Ollama.

entries.name: TOON
entries.use_for: Encode JSON for LLM prompts in a compact, token-efficient format
entries.why: Token-Oriented Object Notation spec with TS SDK and CLI; cuts prompt tokens for tabular/structured data vs JSON, with benchmarks.
entries.summary: Token-Oriented Object Notation: a compact, lossless encoding of the JSON data model combining indentation for nesting with CSV-style tables for uniform arrays, to cut LLM prompt tokens. Has a spec, TS SDK and CLI.
entries.best_for: Feeding uniform, tabular JSON data to LLMs with fewer tokens.
entries.not_for: Gains shrink for deeply nested or non-uniform data, where JSON may be better. Format is stable but still evolving.

entries.name: TurboQuant+
entries.use_for: Shrink the transformer KV cache 3.8-6.4x to fit longer contexts in local LLM inference.
entries.why: Research home for KV cache compression that has been merged upstream into vLLM and llama.cpp.
entries.summary: Python reference implementation of TurboQuant, with a llama.cpp port (Metal, CUDA, HIP) and extra findings such as asymmetric K/V and boundary V. It compresses the KV cache using PolarQuant and Walsh-Hadamard rotation.
entries.best_for: Running long contexts on limited memory, or studying KV cache quantization with benchmarks and papers.
entries.not_for: A turnkey inference engine. The README says it is the research home; run it through llama.cpp or vLLM instead.

entries.name: Vercel AI SDK
entries.use_for: Call any LLM provider from TypeScript with streaming, tool calls, structured output and React/Svelte/Vue chat hooks.
entries.why: Provider-agnostic TS toolkit with first-class UI hooks; the de facto default for AI features in Next.js and other JS apps.
entries.summary: Provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit (AI SDK): generateText, streaming, tool calling, structured output and agents, with UI hooks for React, Svelte, Vue, Angular. Defaults to the Vercel AI Gateway or connects directly via provider packages.
entries.best_for: AI features in Next.js or other JS apps with streaming chat UIs.
entries.not_for: TypeScript/JS only. The default gateway routing is a Vercel service, though direct provider packages avoid it.

entries.name: vLLM
entries.use_for: Serve open-weight LLMs at high throughput behind an OpenAI-compatible API
entries.why: De facto standard for self-hosted GPU LLM serving (PagedAttention, continuous batching)
entries.summary: High-throughput LLM inference and serving engine with PagedAttention, continuous batching, prefix caching, many quantization formats, speculative decoding and an OpenAI-compatible server across NVIDIA, AMD and other hardware.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted production serving of open-weight models on GPUs.
entries.not_for: Needs GPU infrastructure and tuning; overkill for laptop use (Ollama, llama.cpp).

entries.name: vLLM-Omni
entries.use_for: Serve text, image, audio, video and action models with vLLM-style efficient inference.
entries.why: Extends vLLM to diffusion transformers and other non-autoregressive models with staged, disaggregated pipelines.
entries.summary: vLLM-Omni extends vLLM from text generation to omni-modality serving. It uses vLLM's KV cache management for autoregressive stages, adds support for DiT and parallel generation models and overlaps pipeline stages for throughput.
entries.best_for: Teams serving multimodal or diffusion models at scale who already know vLLM.
entries.not_for: A serving runtime that needs GPU or NPU hardware. Not a client SDK.

entries.name: WebLLM
entries.use_for: Run LLMs fully in the browser via WebGPU with an OpenAI-style API.
entries.why: Leading in-browser inference engine; no server needed, so it suits private or offline AI features in web apps.
entries.summary: In-browser LLM inference using WebGPU, with an OpenAI-compatible API (streaming, JSON mode, seeding) and no server. Companion to MLC LLM, with example apps and WebLLM Chat.
entries.best_for: Private or offline AI features running entirely client-side in the browser.
entries.not_for: Needs WebGPU-capable browsers and downloads model weights to the client; limited to smaller models. Function calling is listed as work in progress.
